reasons.C: Short aphoristic sentences alternating with longer ones, dry irony and a homely fire-and-building figure echo the passage's epigrammatic, wry stance and period diction most closely.
reasons.A: Period diction and some wry turns ('the glories make the better story') fit, but the sentences run more evenly and expository, without the author's quick aphoristic jabs.
reasons.B: Modern, earnest register ('cohort', 'face squarely', 'did not bury anyone') and even, explanatory rhythm with no irony or punchy aphorism feel furthest from the author.
